issues.legal_issue: A constitutional challenge to rent-control provisions cannot be considered in appellate or revisional proceedings arising from rent-fixation orders when the original statutory authority lacked jurisdiction to decide that challenge.
material_facts: Rent-fixation proceedings had begun under an earlier rent-control statute and were continued under that statute after it was repealed, pursuant to transitional provisions.
The landlord argued that the transitional provisions requiring pending cases to be decided under the earlier statute violated the constitutional guarantee of equality.
The challenge was raised in proceedings reviewing rent-fixation orders made by the Rent Controller, an authority that could not determine the constitutional validity of the provisions it applied.
issues.conclusion: The constitutional challenge could not be considered in proceedings arising from the Rent Controller’s orders; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A reviewing court cannot consider a constitutional challenge in proceedings arising from an order of a statutory authority when deciding the validity of the legislation was outside that authority’s jurisdiction. The Court applied the principle in K.S. Venkataraman & Co. v. State of Madras, Commissioner of Income-tax, Madhya Pradesh v. Straw Products Ltd., Bhopal, and C.T. Senthilnathan Chettiar v. State of Madras, extending it from proceedings under taxing statutes to rent-fixation proceedings.

predicates.rent_fixation_review: The proceeding is an appeal or revision arising from an order fixing rent under a statute.
predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A party asks the reviewing court to hold a statutory provision constitutionally invalid.
predicates.original_authority_lacks_power_to_decide: The authority that made the order had no jurisdiction to determine the constitutional validity of the provision it applied.
predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge_not_co: The reviewing court does not consider the constitutional validity challenge in that proceeding.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge is made in a review of a statutory rent-fixation order and the original authority could not decide that challenge, the reviewing court does not consider it in that proceeding.
